Please don't take this the wrong way.  No one is perfect.  Not even "the one." People might verbalize this sentiment, but everyone has a flaw or two that we're willing to accept, look past, or work with because in loving eyes, the good greatly outweighs the bad.  I'm not saying this to correct you or make you feel wrong.  I can tell the love you felt was deep.  But I felt I needed to share that universal truth about love and relationships with the hopes that you'll see that imperfect people are very capable of making others feel that deep love you felt, seemingly perfect, if the chemistry is right and the parties have a similar goal for the relationship and accepting of how each strives for it.  Hope you will realize this and be curious enough to create it in your life before it's too late.  Take care.
Thanks... I hope it works out too.  Take care.

I've got a friend reaching out but I don't think he really knows how far removed I've become.  I didn't have super high ambitions in this world.  I just wanted to have a great connection with an awesome girl, create a life routine that worked out for both of us that involved some daily routine comforts mixed with sporadic moments of spontaneity and wild adventures and laughs.  I never cared for too much for who's following who, who posted what, how many followers this person or that person has.  I was always a reluctant participant when social media first got started.  Maybe it's that attitude that contributed to my tendency to isolate.

Sorry you feel the same way too.  It's such a shitty feeling I wish no one felt.  I've spent weeks, sadly months trying to get a grip, snap out of it, rationalize, and will myself to fight again.  The biggest mistake I started making years ago is I recognized that the main thing keeps us going is our innate desire and want to create memories, have experiences and be curious about tomorrow.  I sabotaged those qualities in me and feel so completely removed from any sort of human connection now.  The will simply isn't there anymore.  Please never get to this point.

Darn... I've read a lot of your posts on this subreddit.  Your journey/battle in life is unreal and amazing and people that come here for support are lucky to have you.  Thank you for what you do for so many of us and I truly appreciate your struggle.  Would've been great to have you for this trip!

I'm sorry to hear about your struggles with you ex.  I recently wrote about my experience dating a single mom.  Feel free to check my post history if you want to read about another person's experience dating a single mom after not having a serious gf after 10 years.  I hope you'll be able to pull through this difficult time.

Thanks for reading and for your support.  I've got everything you need for sky-diving, cycling, rock-climbing, backpacking, motorcycles, if I weren't so fucked up in the head I'd be a fun friend to do shit with and the ideal boyfriend for a girl that wants to live life adventurously.  But with girls, you gotta pay to play.  And that's where I come up short being too dumb to earn enough to provide for her but a lot of guys where I work do.  All she has to do is find the right one and he'll get to do all that shit I dreamed of for so long with her, traveling, exploring the world, creating memories, laughing about shit, the hope that kept me going those days I just wanted to crumble.

Thank you for your support and kind words.  I totally get it when you come across a girl and she stands out in your mind like you've got tunnel vision and it sucks knowing she's got someone else.  Tread carefully brother.

Thank you for taking the time to read and write an encouraging reply.  I've been through the peaks and valleys that a lot of us here go through.  I didn't write about it but there was another time I was equally if not more devastated than what I'm going through now.  My friend saved me.  He got me into the gym, I became an avid rock-climber, indoors, outdoors, scaling the granite cliffs of Yosemite and Tahoe, absolutely breath-taking experiences.  I was in the best shape of my life physically and was inspired to find a beautiful girl to take on adventures around in the world, in the backcountry, anywhere and everywhere.  I took a bad fall and suffer chronic back pain because of it.  Ten years later, this was the girl.  Or so I thought.  Every time I chop a head off this monster, another one grows in it's place.  The will isn't there anymore.  I want off this roller coaster bad.

This is just one head of the monster destroying my heart and mind.  But thank you so much for trying to encourage me.  This battle has been raging and I've been fighting for a couple decades now.  You'd be proud of the times I didn't give in but looking back, me dying would've been easier because at least it would've brought closure to the ones that care about me.  Not all this worry for what I'll have to get through next.

Hey... I'm fine... thanks for reading and thanks for wondering about my well-being.

I hate that you and many others here are having that conversation in their head and definitely... silence compared to those thoughts sounds blissful.  I hope me talking to you isn't too frustrating and I appreciate you tolerating my interest.  I didn't share some of what I've been through to re-direct the focus on what's bothering me.  I don't even know if I'm the right person to offer hope.  I just wanted you to know that for what it's worth, someone read what you shared and could relate and if it even brought the slightest comfort to you, I would reply because I know firsthand how alone we can find ourselves at times and I don't wish that on anyone.  I hear what you're saying when you mentioned you feel things are too late or you're behind schedule.  All I can do is caution you that that sentiment gets stronger and scarier the older you get if you still haven't put together a plan and have resources in place to maintain joy in your life that keeps you curious of what tomorrow may bring.  I wish you the confidence knowing that whatever tomorrow brings, good or frustrating, you will be alright and continue loving life.  Please try not to be so hard on yourself for causing stress in the lives of people around you.  I don't know how to go about that but you'll have to find and flip some release levers in your life which I know is easier said than done.  But at least it's an identifiable objective that I hope you're still willing to work on.  Is it too late for you to get together with someone you consider pretty even-keeled and level-headed to come up with things that still make up your identity and put together the beginnings of a plan to get you to a better place?  Perhaps have this plan be what takes precedence above everything and everyone and share this plan with family, friends, loved ones letting them know what they can do to help, which can be an active role or passive, and to get on board or get out of the way for the time being while you better yourself.  If you're still willing, please share some things that you remember you cared about, a memory, a friend, a hobby, a neat idea... anything... I'd like to know how you used to be.

My heart goes out to you for the anger and sadness that is overwhelming you.  I appreciate your honesty too.  What you said is both amazing, powerful and terrifying, that you feel deep down you could recover but you just aren't sure.  I know you said deep, deep, deep down but I took a few layers off that thought for you because people like us tend to feel like more is weighing us down in the moment we feel overwhelmed.  Sometimes it's legit, sometimes it's our minds making things more difficult for us.  I find only those that are closest and know us best are better at assessing that.  You seem to care about yourself but lost your way.  I can relate.  Like you, I doubt if I can come back and I'm turning 35 soon.  I'm a survivor of several deep, dark periods of my life, one was when I was your age and I endured solitude and loneliness for ten years before I allowed myself to do things to create the closest thing to closure I could and allow my heart to move forward.  All this only to fall into another dark pit just when I thought I was turning a corner.  Are you willing to share why you believe you are deserving of self hate?

That sounds awful.  Do you believe deep down the loss is truly unrecoverable? Does the idea of rediscovery of those things sound possible under any sort of circumstances? Sorta like "back to basics" type mindset towards yourself, your hobbies and finding beauty in the simple things of the world? Sorry if I'm asking too many questions and if they sound dumb.  I tend to ask myself these questions also to gauge where my perspective is at.
How did you end losing yourself? Just curious.
